:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.5`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noVueUselessVBind`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`vue`](/linter/domains#vue)
- Sources: 
  - Inspired from [`vue/no-useless-v-bind`](https://eslint.vuejs.org/rules/no-useless-v-bind)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noVueUselessVBind": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow `v-bind` directives whose value is a fixed string.

A `v-bind` directive, written as `v-bind:name` or `:name`, sets an attribute to the result of
a JavaScript expression. When that expression is a fixed string, such as `'foo'`, the
directive always produces the same value. A plain attribute like `id="foo"` does the same
thing and is easier to read.

The rule doesn't report directives with modifiers, such as `:id.prop="'foo'"`, because
modifiers change how Vue applies the value. It also skips elements inside a `v-pre`
element, where Vue leaves the template as written.

## Examples

### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <div :id="'foo'" />
</template>
```

### Valid

```vue
<template>
  <div id="foo" />
  <div :id="foo" />
  <div :id="'foo' + bar" />
  <div :id="`foo-${bar}`" />
  <div :id.prop="'foo'" />
</template>
```

## Options

### `ignoreComments`

Default: `false`

When `true`, the rule doesn't report a directive whose value contains a comment.

```json title='biome.json'
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noVueUselessVBind": {
					"level": "on",
					"options": {
						"ignoreComments": true
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

```

```vue
<template>
  <div :id="'foo'" />
</template>
```

#### Valid

```vue
<template>
  <div :id="'foo' /* used by the tests */" />
</template>
```

### `ignoreStringEscapes`

Default: `false`

When `true`, the rule doesn't report a directive whose string contains an escape sequence
for a special character, such as `\n` for a line break or `\x41` for a character code. A
plain attribute can't contain these escape sequences.

```json title='biome.json'
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noVueUselessVBind": {
					"level": "on",
					"options": {
						"ignoreStringEscapes": true
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

```

#### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <div :title="'It\'s here'" />
</template>
```
